headline: Pilbara Minerals crashes 8% on lithium woes while Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon AI model beats GPT-6 — and the RBA looks increasingly likely to hike rates in November.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a rough session today, dropping 8% to $2.75. There's no single breaking news catalyst, but lithium prices remain deeply depressed and market sentiment toward lithium miners continues to sour. The stock is now down nearly 60% from your entry — the long-term thesis depends on an EV-driven lithium recovery that simply hasn't arrived yet.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped almost 3% last night. The overhang comes partly from news that Rockstar Games employees in the UK are moving toward a union vote — a potential complication ahead of the GTA VI launch window. Despite the dip, Bank of America has been recommending the stock as a buy ahead of GTA VI, citing long-term upside.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped 1.2% today. Ironically, the pullback comes the same day Google unveiled its Gemini 4 Carbon model — but the broader AI ETF space saw some profit-taking. The fund holds a basket of global AI-exposed companies, so short-term swings are normal. The long-term AI buildout story remains intact.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 1% today, dragged by ongoing uncertainty around China's economy and geopolitical tensions. Emerging markets are sensitive to global risk sentiment, and the Iran war situation keeping traders cautious didn't help.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG bounced 1.6% last night, recovering from an initial post-earnings sell-off. Q3 results showed a profit miss and ad revenue slowdown that spooked traders initially, but Google Cloud grew 103% — a standout number — and investors came around. The launch of Gemini 4 Carbon today, which beats GPT-6 on most benchmarks, adds further momentum to the AI story.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.32% today — a quiet, steady session. As a diversified fund holding global and Aussie shares, bonds and property, it tends to smooth out the daily noise. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was essentially flat last night, down just 0.06%. Q3 earnings showed strong cloud growth and healthy cash flow, easing fears about big AI spending. The market liked what it saw overall, even if the share price barely moved — that's a sign of stability after a solid earnings report.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS barely moved today, down 0.08%. It tracks the entire US share market, which was broadly steady last night. Steady as she goes.

movers.name: DHHF (BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF)
movers.note: DHHF was essentially unchanged today, off just 0.02 cents. As an all-in-one globally diversified growth ETF, this is exactly the kind of boring stability you want from a core holding. Nothing to report.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) — another ugly day
watch_today.detail: PLS dropped 8% today to $2.75, and you're now sitting on a 59% loss from your entry. The lithium market is in a prolonged slump with no clear floor in sight. As a long-term holder, the question is whether the thesis — that EV demand eventually rescues lithium prices — still holds. It might, but the timeline keeps stretching. This one warrants a hard think: if you wouldn't buy it at $2.75 today, it's worth considering why you're still holding.

watch_today.title: GOOG — earnings digest and Gemini 4 Carbon momentum
watch_today.detail: GOOG bounced 1.6% last night after an initial post-earnings wobble. Q3 showed Google Cloud growing 103% year-on-year, which is extraordinary. Ad revenue growth was softer than hoped, but that's a short-term headwind. Today Google also unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, a new frontier AI model that reportedly beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 on most benchmarks — and at a lower price. For a long-term holder, this is a positive signal that Google's AI investment is starting to pay off. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA VI union risk is worth watching
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell nearly 3% last night. The new wrinkle: Rockstar Games UK employees are voting on whether to form what could be the largest video game union in UK history — and this is happening right in the GTA VI launch window. Union formation could add costs or delays. Bank of America still recommends buying ahead of GTA VI. As a long-term holder, the union situation is one to watch but not panic over — the GTA VI launch is still the big catalyst that matters.

watch_today.title: RBA November rate hike looking increasingly likely
watch_today.detail: CommBank economists today formally forecast the RBA will raise interest rates in November. Fresh inflation data has surprised to the upside, and even the Treasury chief has admitted government spending is adding to demand. A rate hike would put more pressure on mortgage holders and could slow the economy. For your portfolio, higher rates tend to weigh on growth stocks and ETFs in the short term — but for a long-term holder, this is background noise rather than a reason to change course.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — dipped today but the AI story just got bigger
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF slipped 1.2% today despite Google dropping a bombshell new model (Gemini 4 Carbon) that outperforms GPT-6 on most benchmarks. Short-term volatility in AI-themed funds is normal. The long-term case — that AI infrastructure and software spending will keep growing — looks stronger today, not weaker. Hold and be patient.

watch_today.title: Iran war risk — oil holding above $100/barrel
watch_today.detail: Crude oil is sitting at $101.93/barrel as the US warns Gulf states of a possible short, intense renewal of US-Iran fighting after the US midterm elections. Vice President Vance is making diplomatic outreach to Tehran, and Gulf states are working on a multi-part peace deal — but Iran says it sees 'only unacceptable ideas' so far. If fighting resumes, oil could spike sharply, lifting inflation globally. Watch this space over the next fortnight.

world.summary: The biggest global stories today: the Iran war situation is at a knife's edge ahead of US midterms, a Brazilian political crisis unfolds, a US judge blocks Trump officials from segregating California ballots, and India's Jio Platforms joins the world's top 5 telcos.

stories.title: US warns of possible short, intense Iran war renewal after midterms — diplomacy racing to prevent it
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has privately warned Gulf states that a short but intense military confrontation with Iran could resume after the November midterm elections. Vice President Vance is personally reaching out to Tehran in a last-ditch diplomatic push, while Gulf nations are scrambling to put together a multi-part peace deal. The snag: Iran has told mediators it sees 'only unacceptable ideas' on the table so far. If fighting does resume, expect oil prices — already above $100/barrel — to spike sharply, which would push inflation higher everywhere, including Australia. This is the single biggest geopolitical risk in markets right now.

stories.title: Brazil's Flávio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss
stories.why_it_matters: Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, has fled to the United States after losing his own election. This follows a pattern of Bolsonaro family members and allies facing legal and political pressure in Brazil under the Lula government. The elder Bolsonaro himself faces ongoing legal challenges. The political crisis in Latin America's largest economy — a key trading partner and commodity producer — is worth watching for anyone with emerging market exposure (like VGE.AX).

stories.title: US judge rejects Trump officials' bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
stories.source: The New York Times / ABC News
stories.why_it_matters: A federal judge has firmly rejected a request from Trump administration officials to segregate roughly 20,000 California ballots, calling it an 'attempted election interference'. The judge said the request had no legal basis and would have disenfranchised legitimate voters. With US midterm elections approaching, this ruling signals the courts are prepared to push back hard against attempts to manipulate the count — an important guardrail for American democratic processes that global markets are watching closely.

stories.title: Jio Platforms breaks into global top 5 telcos after listing
stories.why_it_matters: India's Jio Platforms — the telecoms and digital services giant owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani — has broken into the global top 5 telcos by market cap following its stock market listing. This is a big deal: Jio has over 400 million subscribers and is rapidly expanding into cloud, AI and digital payments. It signals the growing weight of Indian tech companies on the world stage, and is relevant for anyone holding emerging market funds like VGE.AX, which has India as a major exposure.

stories.title: UK Chancellor gives households £100 to help with 'global economic storms'
stories.why_it_matters: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves (referred to as Healey in the headline) is handing £100 to British households to cushion them against rising global economic pressures. The move comes as inflation remains sticky in the UK and cost-of-living stress persists. It's a reminder that governments worldwide are still fighting inflation aftershocks — and Australia is in the same boat, with the RBA now likely to raise rates next month.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, up 0.5% to close at 8,892. Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ posted modest gains — helped by strong tech earnings from Microsoft and a recovery in Google. Oil eased slightly but remains above $100/barrel. Gold slipped a little. The Aussie dollar is holding steady just above 70 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session today — broad-based gains across most sectors.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Modest gains last night, supported by Microsoft's earnings beat.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech held up well last night despite mixed earnings signals.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Still above $100 — Iran war risk keeping a floor under prices.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Eased slightly but still near historic highs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar steady, just above 70 cents.

politics.summary: A big week for the RBA — markets are now pricing in a rate hike in November after stubbornly high inflation data. Treasurer Chalmers is under fire from economists, and the government has passed a significant online safety bill while backing away from other internet regulation.

stories.title: RBA November rate hike now expected — CommBank leads the call
stories.why_it_matters: CommBank economists have formally forecast the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates at its November meeting — meaning your mortgage repayments could be going up again. The trigger is a surprise spike in inflation data that caught markets off guard. The AFR editorial board argues the RBA 'must pull the trigger', while the Guardian's Greg Jericho warns a rate hike risks pushing unemployment higher. Treasurer Chalmers is also under pressure after the Treasury chief admitted government spending is adding to demand — a key driver of inflation.

stories.title: Chalmers accused of 'spin' as economists push back on inflation narrative
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is copping heat from economists who say he's 'spinning' the inflation story — downplaying the government's role in stoking price pressures through spending. The Australian describes Labor's approach as 'turning up the inflation cooker', while The Nightly says economists have directly called out Chalmers' framing. Chalmers has also lowered expectations for any fuel excise relief, which had been floated as a way to ease cost-of-living pain at the bowser.

stories.title: Albanese's Digital Duty of Care Bill passes the House
stories.why_it_matters: Anthony Albanese's Digital Duty of Care Bill has passed the House of Representatives. The bill targets serious online harm — think cyberbullying, violent content and material targeting children — by placing new legal obligations on social media and digital platforms to protect users. Free speech advocates have raised concerns, saying the law could be used to suppress legitimate speech. The Senate still needs to pass it before it becomes law.

stories.title: Government backs down on separate internet laws
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government has backed down on a separate set of proposed internet regulation laws, distinct from the Duty of Care Bill. The government has been trying to navigate a complex space — cracking down on harmful online content while not being seen to over-regulate free speech. Free speech experts quoted in reports say Australia is becoming 'increasingly undemocratic' in its approach to online regulation. This is a space that tech companies operating in Australia (including Google and Microsoft, which you hold) are watching closely.

ai.summary: Google dropped a major AI bombshell today — its new Gemini 4 Carbon model beats OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude on most benchmarks, and at a lower cost. Apple also unveiled a new AI-boosted iMac. AI regulation is picking up pace globally.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon beats GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 — but you can't try it yet
stories.why_it_matters: Google has officially announced Gemini 4 Carbon, its most powerful AI model yet. According to benchmark tests, it outperforms OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 on the majority of standard AI tests — and critically, it does so at a fraction of the price of its rivals. The catch: it's not available to the public yet, with Google holding it back for reasons that aren't entirely clear. This is directly relevant to your GOOG holding — it shows Google's multi-billion dollar AI investment is producing real, world-leading results.

stories.title: Apple unveils new iMac with M6 chip and major AI capabilities boost
stories.why_it_matters: Apple has launched a new iMac powered by its M6 chip, promising a major jump in performance and on-device AI capabilities. The new machine can run more powerful AI tasks locally — without sending data to the cloud — which Apple is pitching as a privacy advantage over cloud-based AI rivals. This keeps Apple firmly in the AI hardware race alongside Google and Microsoft.

stories.title: Google's TPU chip moment — what it means for the AI race
stories.why_it_matters: Commentary is building around Google's custom AI chips (called TPUs — Tensor Processing Units) giving it a cost advantage in running AI workloads compared to companies reliant on Nvidia hardware. Combined with the Gemini 4 Carbon launch, analysts are comparing this moment to a turning point where Google's vertical integration — owning both the AI software and the chips that run it — could become a meaningful competitive edge against OpenAI and Microsoft.

stories.title: AI regulation heating up globally — US, Switzerland, California all moving
stories.why_it_matters: AI regulation is accelerating on multiple fronts. California has passed two new laws — SB 53 and the TDTA — focused on AI transparency, requiring companies to disclose when AI is being used in decisions that affect people. Switzerland is advancing sector-specific AI rules with voluntary codes of conduct. US tech leaders are now urgently calling for federal AI rules, noting that China already has a comprehensive regulatory framework in place. For investors in AI-exposed stocks, regulation is both a risk (compliance costs) and an opportunity (it legitimises the industry and raises barriers to entry for smaller players).

sport.summary: It's NRL Grand Final week — the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in a thriller. The post-season transfer market is buzzing with the Adam Walker saga dominating headlines. In AFL, the 2027 fixture has dropped and Sydney are the big winners. Plus, a big off-season rugby league-to-rugby union crossover.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over Knights in a thriller at Accor Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters have won the 2026 NRL Grand Final, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a nail-biter at Accor Stadium. One point the difference — it doesn't get closer than that. The Roosters are premiers, capping what must have been a remarkable finals run.

stories.title: Adam Walker saga — who signs him, and the 'most disappointing' part of it all
stories.why_it_matters: The Adam Walker transfer saga is the hottest story in NRL off-season. Fox Sports' Braith Anasta has made a surprise reveal — reportedly Walker 'doesn't want to go' to one of the clubs strongly linked with him. There's also a 'big Bunnies twist' emerging, with South Sydney potentially in the mix. A replacement is also being lined up for the Roosters' halves after the Grand Final, with former Roosters players and coaches weighing in on what's been the 'most disappointing' aspect of the whole saga.

stories.title: Gold Coast Titans punch extend their half's deal until 2029, beating out the Chiefs
stories.why_it_matters: Great local news — the Gold Coast Titans have successfully re-signed one of their key halves until 2029, reportedly fending off interest from the New Zealand Chiefs rugby union franchise. Keeping their spine together is crucial for the Titans as they build for the future. A big retention win for the Gold Coast club.

stories.title: AFL 2027 fixture drops — Sydney the big winner, St Kilda snubbed from primetime
stories.why_it_matters: The 2027 AFL fixture has been released and Sydney Swans are the standout winners — loaded up with prime-time slots and favourable scheduling. St Kilda have been completely shut out of primetime games, a commercial blow for the Saints. Fox Sports has graded every team's fixture, with some clubs getting clear advantages in travel and rest days heading into the new season.

stories.title: NRL star joins returning Wallabies in Michael Cheika's Waratahs squad
stories.why_it_matters: Michael Cheika, back coaching the NSW Waratahs, has attracted an NRL star to make the code switch and join a squad that also includes returning Wallabies. The crossover signing is a sign of the Waratahs trying to shake things up under Cheika's influence. Rugby union has been increasingly competitive in luring NRL talent, particularly with Pacific Island players who have options across both codes.
